convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to invoke the AdaptiveRenko custom indicator, which is not a built-in MT5 indicator. The Renko brick logic and adaptive period calculation require understanding the custom indicator's internals to replicate in Python.

derived_values.name: Renko brick reversal detection
derived_values.formula: Direction change between consecutive Renko bricks

other_exits: MMRec-based partial close: money management recommendation system can suggest reducing position size at certain profit/loss thresholds
Duplex mode: opposite signal closes current position before opening new one in reverse direction

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMRec system recommends lot size based on account equity and risk parameters; negative input values treated as fixed lots, positive values as deposit fraction for money management

custom_logic_notes: Duplex mode means the EA trades both long and short, reversing on signal change rather than just closing. The MMRec (Money Management Recommendation) module adjusts lot size dynamically based on account state - it can recommend reducing or increasing exposure. The Adaptive Renko indicator constructs bricks dynamically based on ATR volatility, so the effective 'bar' is a Renko brick, not a time-based bar. Signal is read from iCustom buffer values representing brick direction (up=buffer0, down=buffer1). Digit adjustment is applied: SL and TP in points are multiplied by 10 when _Digits==5 or _Point<0.001.
python_conversion_notes: The Adaptive Renko indicator must be reimplemented in Python first - it uses ATR to dynamically set brick sizes and then constructs Renko bricks from raw price data. This is non-trivial as Renko construction is stateful (each brick depends on the previous brick close). The MMRec module needs careful porting as it references account equity and margin. Entry signals are based on Renko brick direction changes (reversal pattern), not standard time-bar crossovers. Use tick data for accurate Renko brick construction. The duplex logic (close opposite + enter new) must preserve atomicity - both operations should be treated as one logical trade to avoid orphaned positions.
